I am a 22 year old female who has been dealing with depression and anxiety problems for a majority of my life. I've been diagnosed and seen countless doctors, but I won't get into all of that right now. Instead I will try and keep my introduction a bit more positive. I am in grad school and I nanny. I have a dog who is more scared of the world than I am, so we spend a lot of time cuddled up in bed together. I spend a decent amount of time drawing and writing, which also helps with my emotions. I have no idea what else to say since that sums up my current life, so feel free to ask me about myself, and tell me about you! I look forward to being part of this community.

Welcome raindrop!

I look forward to your efforts to expand awareness about our little space, here. I've reached out a bit in the past, but imagine in the coming days/months/years that more and more traffic will start to show up from various places. And I'm sure there will be the bad that comes along with the good experiences here. But overall, I made this sub so that people could have a safe place to express whatever they felt about suicide and their own suicidal thoughts, without any of the restrictions imposed by the various other forums around the web.

I'm 35. Both of my parents died a few years back, and as a person interested in existential thought and having a great sense of empathy for others, I find myself heavily burdened by the amount of suffering I see in the world. Suicide, for me, seems like the rational course of action and I think about it daily. I have a pretty heavy staring contest with the pistol next to my bed, almost nightly.

My programmed survival instincts (fear) and the encouragement of a couple of great friends have kept me from it, so far, but I know it will be the choice I make, eventually... if the world doesn't take care of things sooner.

It should go without saying that I don't believe this sub should be a place to encourage individuals to commit the act, but I also don't want this to be yet another place where someone can't feel free to discuss their methods for doing so, so that they can come to terms with the act, once their mind has been made up. And in that same vein, I feel this should be a free place, where someone wouldn't shy away from expressing their exact feelings and thoughts on how, why and when they might act.

All that being said, again, welcome! I look forward to seeing more of your thoughts!
